newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 29.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
* The Federal Trade Commission has accused R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co of illegally enticing minors to smoke with its carton ads of "Joe Camel".
* Lawyers for accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh rested their defense after 3-1/2 days.
* A series of tornadoes cut a destructive swath through Central Texas, killing at least 27 people.

* A coalition of theater owners, producers and union officials is considering launching a $10 million-a-year fund to to promote serious dramas and small musicals in an effort to further revitalize the area.

* Five members of a Hasidic community in New York have been indicted on allegations they defrauded the federal and state governments out of millions of dollars in student loans, business assistance and housing subsidies.
* Cherie Blair, the wife of British Prime Minister Tony Blair, has returned to her real job -- a Queen's Counsel -- after spending two months campaigning for her husband.
* The recent murder of a real estate broker in Central Park hasn't driven away many New Yorkers, who still consider the park safe at night.
